scholarships.name: AUB International Scholarship
scholarships.requirements: Must be an international fee-payer; submission of a high-quality creative portfolio; must hold an offer of study for a full-time BA (Hons) degree; 500-word statement on 'How AUB will help me change the creative industry'.
scholarships.description: This competitive award recognizes exceptional creative talent. It provides a £5,000 reduction in the first year of tuition for undergraduate students who show significant potential in arts, design, or media.

scholarships.name: AUB International Scholarship
scholarships.requirements: Hold an international fee-paying status; minimum 2:1 degree in a related creative field; strong digital portfolio submission; must be a full-time Master's applicant at the Bournemouth campus.
scholarships.description: A merit-based scholarship for international postgraduates aimed at fostering global perspectives within the AUB studio environment. The award is a £3,000 one-off reduction in the total Master's tuition fee.

Overview Foundation Undergraduate Postgraduate Postgraduate (online) Research Overview Foundation Undergraduate Postgraduate Postgraduate (online) Research Home Fees and financial support Undergraduate Fees and financial support : Undergraduate Find out everything you need to know to plan your student finances including tuition fees and living costs Undergraduate Find your tuition fee for Undergraduate degree courses starting in September 2026. Please note that Home and Channel Islands and Isle of Man fees will be subject to increase each year, and International (including EU students) fees are fixed for the duration of your course. Downloads Fees Payment Policy (2026–27) Fees Payment Policy FAQs (2026–27) Undergraduate fees All students are required to pay tuition fees for each academic year of study. Students who enter directly onto Years 2 or 3 of a course will pay Year 1 tuition fees. Current AUB policy is to charge Home fees at the level of the cap set by the government. Home Channel Island and Isle of Man International/EU Home Home Tuition Fee 2027/28 Applicants £10,050 Integrated Foundation Year – all courses £10,050 Optional placement year £2,010* *The tuition fee for the optional placement year is £2,010 , subject to inflationary increases based on government policy, and providing you progress through the course in the normal timeframe (no repeat years or breaks in study). Channel Island and Isle of Man Channel Island and Isle of Man Tuition Fee 2027/28 Applicants £10,050 Integrated Foundation Year – all courses £10,050 Optional placement year £2,010* *The tuition fee for the optional placement year is £2,010 , subject to inflationary increases based on government policy, and providing you progress through the course in the normal timeframe (no repeat years or breaks in study). International/EU International/EU Tuition Fee 2027/28 Applicants (all years) £19,950 Integrated Foundation Year – all courses £19,950 Optional placement year £2,010* *The tuition fee for the optional placement year is £2,010 , subject to inflationary increases based on government policy, and providing you progress through the course in the normal timeframe (no repeat years or breaks in study). International scholarships FdA fees Home Channel Islands and Isle of Man Home Home Tuition Fee 2027/28 Applicants £7,950 Channel Islands and Isle of Man Channel Islands and Isle of Man Tuition Fee 2027/28 Applicants £7,950 Undergraduate financial support Home Channel Islands and Isle of Man N.Ireland, Scotland and Wales International/EU America Home Home Student Loans Company (SLC) The SLC works with Student Finance England, Student Finance Wales, the Student Awards Agency for Scotland, Higher Education Institutions and HMRC to provide support for British and EU students in the UK. SLC support includes loans to cover the cost of tuition fees, as well as maintenance loans to contribute towards living costs whilst at University. For undergraduate students who've arranged an SLC loan to cover the cost of tuition fees, the SLC will pay the loan directly to AUB. For undergraduate students, all other SLC maintenance loans will be paid directly to the student. For undergraduate students, any other fees due to the University will need to be paid directly by the student. For further information about SLC support and for details on how to apply, please visit the GOV.UK website . Maintenance loan Maintenance loans are available for each year of study to help with living costs such as food, accommodation and travel. The amount you can borrow depends on where you live and study, and your household income. For more information and to find out what support you could get, please use the Student Finance Calculator on gov.uk. Bursaries and additional support To be eligible for support, you must be in receipt of a full maintenance loan from Student Finance England, with a net household income of £25,000 or less. Our support offer is based on household income information provided by Student Finance England and eligibility is verified annually. What you’re entitled to receive will depend on your precise individual circumstances. Please note: financial support and bursaries offered under AUB’s Access and Participation Plans aren't available to students studying at franchise partner institutions. Travel costs to attend Open Days or Offer Holder Days If you're in receipt of Free School Meals, we may be able to offer you financial support to help cover the costs of attending an Open Day in person at AUB. We have an annual fund, the AUB Applicant Access Bursary, available for you to receive a one-off award of up to £75 for travel costs to attend an Open Day. Eligible students will receive emails on this support as part of their Open Day communications. If you’re an AUB Contextual Offer Holder , the AUB Applicant Access Bursary is also available for you to receive a one-off award of up to £75 for travel costs to attend Offer Holder Days and university induction/transition events. You'll receive emails on how to apply for this for eligible activities, but if you have any questions, please contact the Access and Participation team . You can find out more about the Applicant Access Bursary, including terms and conditions, on our website . Accommodation costs If you’re an undergraduate student in your first year (Integrated Foundation Year (Year 0) or Level 4) living in AUB’s student accommodation, you’ll receive an accommodation bursary of £1,000. You don't need to apply for this bursary as it'll be paid automatically to eligible students. Please note: this funding is only available during your first year of undergraduate study at AUB. Support for students who are care experienced or estranged A bursary of £2,000 per annum. This isn't means-tested and is in addition to any other bursaries and benefits that you may be entitled to. If you think you may be eligible for this bursary, find out more information on how to apply and the support we offer . Students eligible for this bursary may also be eligible for the AUB Guarantor Award . Support for students who are young adult carers A bursary of £2,000 per annum. This isn't means-tested and is in addition to any other bursaries and benefits that you may be entitled to. If you think you may be eligible for this bursary, find out more information on how to apply and the support we offer . Support for disabled students If you’re required to make a £200 contribution towards a laptop previously provided through DSA, AUB will pay this £200. In addition, we provide support for the cost of Educational Psychologist reports where required. This is in addition to any other bursaries or benefits that you may be entitled to. For more information, please contact the Student Services Team . Travel costs If you’re an undergraduate student in your second year (Level 5) or third year (Level 6) you’ll receive a £200 payment to assist with travel costs associated with your studies. You don't need to apply for this bursary as it'll be paid automatically to eligible students. Opportunities linked to graduate employment If you're in second year (Level 5) or third year (Level 6), we have an annual fund, the AUB Employability Bursary, available for you to receive a one-off award of up to £300 for: Travel and accommodation costs for interviews, internships and other opportunities Attendance fees for courses, conferences or residential training events Smart clothing Application costs for further study Specialist equipment (not including laptops, computers or books) Some costs associated with the course Other expenses related to engagement with opportunities in the creative industries Please note: you can apply for this award in either second or third year. However, this is a one-off award, so if you apply for it in second year, you won't be able to apply again in third year. Non-AUB support and information You can find out more about non-AUB grants, bursaries and scholarships on the Save the Student website. Access and Participation Plan 2024/25 – 2027/28 Channel Islands and Isle of Man Channel Islands and Isle of Man Students from the Islands are subject to different funding arrangements and support to mainland UK students. Guernsey The state of Guernsey offers higher education student grants to help with the cost of tuition fees, living and travel. The amount of funding available depends on a number of factors – including an assessment of your parents’ income. Bursaries may also be available to independent students who have no support from parents. To find out more, please visit the Guernsey Government website . Jersey The state of Jersey offers funding for higher education students to help with living costs and tuition fees. The amount of funding available depends on an assessment of your parents’ income or, if you’re an independent student, your own household income. The amount of funding you can receive for tuition fees also depends on what type of course you’re taking and where you’re taking it. Find out more on the Jersey Government website . Isle of Man Students from the Isle of Man aren't eligible for a loan from the UK Student Loans Company, but the Isle of Man government offers higher education students a grand (Student Award) to help with living cost and tuition. The amount of funding you can receive is dependent on your parents’ income or, if you’re an independent student, your own household income, as well as the type of course you're taking and where you're taking it. Find out more on the Isle of Man Government website . N.Ireland, Scotland and Wales Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales If you normally live in Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales, you can follow the links below to find out what funding support is available to you. The support available varies, so it’s important that you check the correct country. Northern Ireland Students who normally live in Northern Ireland may receive financial support for university from the Northern Ireland Executive. For more information, students should refer to the student finance for Northern Ireland website . Scotland Students who normally live in Scotland may receive financial support for university from the Scottish Government. For more information, students should refer to the student finance for Scotland website . Wales Students who normally live in Wales may receive financial support for university from the Welsh Assembly Government. For more information, students should refer to the student finance for Wales website . International/EU International/EU If you are unsure whether you should be classed as an ‘International/EU’ or a ‘Home’ student, please complete and return the fees assessment form . Further advice on fee status can also be found on the UKCISA website . Norwegian students are eligible for financial support from The Norwegian State Educational Loan Fund, administered by Lanekassen, which provides student loans and stipends for higher education. For further information on the Loan Fund visit the Lanekassen website. Icelandic students can borrow loans via The Icelandic Student Loan Fund (Menntasjodur). Visit the Menntasjodur website for more information about Icelandic student loans. America Loans for American Students Students from America will be pleased to know that United States Federal Loans are available for you to study at Arts University Bournemouth, just as they would be if you were studying in the US as AUB has been authorised to certify applications. Fees and financial support : Support for students who are care-experienced, estranged, and young adult carers Find out everything you need to know to plan your student finances including tuition fees and living costs Support for students who are care-experienced, estranged, and young adult carers Here at AUB, we offer support to undergraduate students who are care-experienced, estranged, and young adult carers. For students in this position who are considering applying to AUB, or want to find out more about us, the Access and Participation Team offer individual pre-application visits, providing the opportunity to see the campus and meet our staff and students. You can also email us at wp@aub.ac.uk with any questions and we’ll be happy to help! Once you join us at AUB as a student, a member of the Wellbeing Team will be the your key contact, with a dedicated lead contact depending on which bursary you're receiving. Bursaries Support for students who are care-experienced The Care Leavers bursary supports students who've been in care prior to coming to AUB. Support for students who are estranged The Stand Alone Bursary supports students who are estranged from both of their biological or adoptive parents. Support for young adult carers The Young Carers Bursary is for people aged 18-25 who care for a friend or family member who can't cope without their support. If you have any questions about criteria or the application process, please email AUB’s Access and Participation Team who'll be able to advise you on how to apply for the bursary and how we assess the application. The team will also be a point of contact for you throughout your time at AUB and will meet with you at least three times during the academic year ahead of each bursary payment. Throughout your time at AUB, the Wellbeing Team will be able to refer you to the many sources of advice and support available while you’re studying and encourage you to achieve your study goals. You'll be also given the opportunity to apply to work as an Outreach Ambassador , carrying out paid work with young people from schools and colleges who are thinking about studying at university. Bursary FAQs Who is my lead contact for the bursary? Before you become an AUB student, please contact the Access and Participation Team Once you become an AUB student, you'll have a lead contact in the Wellbeing Team Am I eligible for the bursary? To be eligible for the Care Leaver, Stand Alone or Young Adult Carer bursary, you must be 25 or under, domiciled to England and registered with Student Finance England. This isn't a means-tested bursary and is in addition to any other bursaries and benefits that you may be entitled to. Please note: financial support and bursaries offered under AUB’s Access and Participation Plans aren't available to students studying at franchise partner institutions. Eligibility and application evidence related to each of the three bursaries can be found in the Bursaries section above. Please click on the bursary you're considering applying for further details. Who do you accept evidence of my situation from? On the application form you will be asked to provide the contact details of a professional that can confirm your eligibility for your bursary. This could be: A local authority representative A teacher from your school or college Your GP Another professional person who's unrelated to you How to apply You will need to wait until you have completed the enrolment process in September at AUB to apply for the bursary. If you have identified yourself on your UCAS application form as a student that may be care experienced, estranged or a young adult carer you will receive an email from the Access and Participation Team ( wp@aub.ac.uk ) to your AUB email address with instructions on how to apply once applications have opened for your academic year of study. The application form can be found on e-vision on your My AUB Dashboard. Please use your AUB email address on your application form. This will also be the email address we use to contact you to confirm the status of your bursary application and for communications about your bursary meetings. Once your eligibility has been confirmed, you'll be e-introduced to the Wellbeing Team with information on your bursary meetings and support available. How is the bursary paid? The bursary is worth £2,000 a year and is paid in three instalments after a Bursary meeting with your named contact and confirmation that you are engaging and attending your studies. The first instalment paid in the Autumn Term is 25% (£500), the second instalment paid in the Spring Term is 50% (£1,000) and third instalment paid in the Summer Term is 25% (£500). The bursary is paid directly into your bank account that is linked to your Student Finance England account. Is there additional financial support available? As well as our bursaries we have a range of financial support available for undergraduate students in receipt of a full maintenance loan from Student Finance England, with a net household income of £25,000 or less. Our support offer is based on household income information provided by Student Finance England and eligibility is verified annually. What you’re entitled to receive will depend on your precise, individual circumstances. For further details of the undergraduate student financial support available please visit our undergraduate fees and financial support webpage. Can I apply for a bursary part way through my studies? Yes – if you found out about the bursary and your eligibility later in the year, or if your situation has changed, we're still here to support you. If you're applying part way through the academic year, or you are in your second or third year of undergraduate studies, you'll find the application form on e-vision on your My AUB Dashboard. International Scholarships We aim to have a diverse student environment with the best creative talent in the UK. To support our goal of a multicultural campus, Arts University Bournemouth (AUB) is pleased to offer several awards which may come in the form of bursaries, fee waivers and scholarships. There will be a simple scholarship application form for you to complete. This form will be available to you after you receive an offer of admission from AUB. All AUB awards are offered on a first come, first served basis. If you do not qualify for a scholarship or bursary, you can take advantage of the Early Payment Fee Waiver, which is available to all who qualify. Each student will only qualify for one scholarship, bursary or fee waiver – they cannot be stacked. If a student is enrolled part-time, scholarships, bursaries, and fee waivers may be pro-rated to the yearly tuition fees. To help you plan and budget your finances during your time at AUB, as an international student, we've created a Cost of Living guide . If you'd like to discuss any of these financial awards or discuss any financial matters, get in touch with our International team who'll be able to help. Please note: all international scholarships are for on-campus courses only and do not apply to online courses. International Undergraduate and Postgraduate Scholarships International Undergraduate and Postgraduate Scholarships Our international scholarships are awarded to recognise and support creative talent within the global international student community. AUB Progression Bursaries AUB Progression Bursaries Progression Bursaries are available for all AUB students who wish to progress onto an Undergraduate or Postgraduate Programme Early Payment Fee Waiver Early Payment Fee Waiver Available to students who have accepted their offer onto a Foundation, Undergraduate or Postgraduate course for every year of their studies. Creative Start – AUB Foundation Diploma Scholarship Creative Start – AUB Foundation Diploma Scholarship This scholarship is available to support studies on our Foundation Diploma in Art and Design. Postgraduate Scholarships for EU Nationals Postgraduate Scholarships for EU Nationals This scholarship can support your studies on one of our postgraduate degrees. British National Residing Overseas British National Residing Overseas Supporting your studies at AUB on one of our Foundation, Undergraduate or Postgraduate degrees External scholarships There are a number of external scholarships that you may also may be eligible to apply for: Chevening Scholarship Funded by the UK Foreign and Commonwealth Office and partner organisations, Chevening provides fully-funded scholarships, leaving you free to focus on achieving your academic goals and enjoying the experience of a lifetime. You will live and study in the UK for a year, during which time you will develop professionally and academically, grow your network, experience UK culture, and build lasting positive relationships. Level: Postgraduate for any subject area Apply on the Chevening website Information for students from Ukraine All students are considered for all AUB scholarships, regardless of nationality. Please refer to the UKCISA website , which is being continually updated with information for Ukrainian Nationals about the Ukrainian schemes Information on external global scholarships can also be found on the British Council’s Study UK website . Progression Bursaries Progression Bursaries are available for all students who have completed either our Foundation Diploma or an Undergraduate degree and wish to progress onto an Undergraduate or Postgraduate programme. Find out more about the eligibility criteria and application process for each of our Progression Bursaries below. Summer School to Foundation Studies Foundation to Undergraduate Studies Undergraduate to Postgraduate Studies Summer School to Foundation Studies This award is for students enrolling on the Foundation Diploma at AUB, after having completed a Summer Course or Study Abroad programme at AUB. Eligibility Criteria You must: Be enrolled in or have completed an AUB Summer Course or Study Abroad programme within the past two years. Have been offered a place on the Foundation Diploma at AUB Be classified as an overseas fee payer (international student) for fee purposes. Submit the scholarship application form by the posted deadline. Application and Selection Process The scholarship application form will be forwarded to you by email once you receive an offer of admission. You will need to complete the application form and submit it prior to the application deadline. If you are successful, you will be sent information about the bursary you have been awarded, which will include instructions on how to accept the offer and what you need to do next. Please note, this bursary cannot be combined with any other AUB financial award or scholarship. Summer students applying for Bachelor's degrees? Students who have completed a Summer Course or Study Abroad programme at AUB who apply for Bachelor's degree programmes at AUB should apply for the International Undergraduate Scholarships . Should applicants for Bachelor's degree programmes who have done a Summer Course or Study Abroad programme at AUB not receive the International Undergraduate Scholarship, they will be eligible for the Summer School and Study Abroad progression award of £2,000. Foundation to Undergraduate Studies This award is for students enrolling on an Undergraduate/BA or BSc (Hons) degree programme at AUB who have already completed AUB’s Foundation Diploma. Undergraduate Progression Bursary: £3,000 per annum Fees with Undergraduate Progression Bursary: £16,950 Eligibility Criteria You must: Be a current AUB Foundation Diploma student (or have successfully completed the AUB Foundation Diploma within the last two years). Be classified as an overseas fee payer (international student) for fee purposes. Submit the scholarship application form by the posted deadline. Application and Selection Process The scholarship application form will be forwarded to you by email once you receive an offer of admission. You will need to complete the application form and submit it prior to the application deadline. If you are successful, you will be sent information about the bursary you have been awarded, which will include instructions on how to accept the offer and what you need to do next. Please note, this bursary cannot be combined with any other AUB financial award or scholarship. Undergraduate to Postgraduate Studies This award is for students who have completed an Undergraduate/BA or BSc (Hons) degree at AUB and are progressing to a Postgraduate/MA course at AUB. Postgraduate Progression Bursary: £5,000 per annum for MA courses taught on campus, or £1,995 for online MA courses. Fees with Postgraduate Progression Bursary: £14,950 (on-campus courses); £7,980 (online) Eligibility Criteria You must: Be a current AUB Undergraduate student or have completed an AUB Undergraduate degree in the past two years. Have been offered a place on a Postgraduate degree at AUB with a start date of either January 2027, September 2027, or January 2028. Be classified as an overseas fee payer (international student) for fee purposes. Submit the scholarship application form by the posted deadline. Application and Selection Process The scholarship application form will be forwarded to you by email once you receive an offer of admission. You will need to complete the application form and submit it prior to the application deadline. If you are successful, you will be sent information about the bursary you have been awarded, which will include instructions on how to accept the offer and what you need to do next. Please note, this bursary cannot be combined with any other AUB financial award or scholarship. Student Finance England Postgraduate students may be able to apply for a postgraduate loan through Student Finance England . Our Master of Architecture course is eligible for funding through the undergraduate funding system. Your personal eligibility will depend upon your undergraduate degree and the time since graduating. UK Government Postgraduate Loans Scheme The Government provides a loan for postgraduate MA study. If a student meets the criteria, the Postgraduate Loan (PGL) will be paid to the student as a contribution towards Tuition Fees, living costs and other course costs. What you need to know: Loans will be available up to a maximum value of £12,858 for 2025/26 and paid directly to the student in three equal instalments per academic year, up to a maximum of two years. Loans will be available to UK Nationals (and individuals with settled status in the UK). Students under 60 will be eligible for MA loans. Loans are available for all our MA programmes, excluding Master of Architecture – students studying full-time, part-time may be eligible. In order to qualify for a part-time MA loan, you need to be studying at least 50% intensity of an equivalent full-time student in the first year of the course. Loans are non-means-tested. Students who already hold an MA qualification (or an equivalent or higher level qualification) won't be eligible for PGL. This applies even if the previous qualification was entirely self-funded and/or achieved outside the UK. Lower level qualifications such as Postgraduate Diplomas or Postgraduate Certificates of Education won't affect eligibility for PGL. Repayments will be income-contingent and made concurrently with undergraduate loans. Rates will be set at 6% of annual income over £21,000. For further information, visit the GOV.UK website . Also refer to the government's guidance on applying for a Master's loan . If you have any questions about your eligibility for the loan please contact Student Finance England . Overview From September 2026, you’ll have the option to undertake a specialised Foundation year in a subject area you’re interested in, setting you up for success on one of Arts University Bournemouth's undergraduate courses. The Integrated Foundation Year, or Year 0, is a chance for you to explore and develop your skills and knowledge at an introductory level before progressing onto your BA/BSc (Hons) degree. By the end of the Foundation year, you’ll have a better understanding of what the subject area has to offer, enabling you to confidently join students on your chosen degree course. The Integrated Foundation Year gives you the chance to get a grounding across several subject areas. How to apply Register your interest Book an Open Day View our prospectus Downloads Course Specification What to expect from an Integrated Foundation Year Throughout the Integrated Foundation Year, you'll learn: How learning is structured in higher education, including expectations around independent study, reflective engagement, and participation in a studio-based learning environment. Core design and creative thinking methods that support idea generation, iteration, and problem-solving across various art, design and media disciplines. Visual literacy and material exploration through playful, critical, and experimental use of both digital and physical methods. Foundational project-management and collaboration skills, including working in teams, planning, communication, and managing simple tasks within a project brief. Academic research and writing skills, developing the ability to build lines of inquiry through observation, contextual research, documentation, and reflective practice. Our courses You’ll need to have an idea of the undergraduate degree you’d like to progress onto after your Integrated Foundation Year, but this isn’t locked down. For instance, you may apply initially to study Content Creation with Marketing but discover a passion for Creative Direction along the way and wish to switch. This will be fine as long as your alternative choice is in the same subject area. Successful completion of the Integrated Foundation Year guarantees progression to Level 4 (first year) of the degree associated with your chosen pathway. Apply now How to apply Application process Entry requirements Fees and financial support Application process To apply for a course with an Integrated Foundation Year, you must select the correct option on UCAS. All courses that include an Integrated Foundation Year will have a separate listing and course code, including with Foundation Year in the course title, (e.g. BA (Hons) Fine Art with Foundation Year). This is the course you should select on your UCAS application. If you have any questions about Integrated Foundation Years or would like to discuss your options, please contact our Admissions team at admissions@aub.ac.uk . Entry requirements UCAS Tariff Applicants should have Level 3 qualifications, which should normally include at least one creative subject. To join the Integrated Foundation Year, we're looking for 32 UCAS Tariff points. You can use the UCAS Tariff Calculator to work out how many points you have. Qualifications For acceptance onto an Integrated Foundation Year, we accept a range of qualifications, including A-Levels, BTEC Extended Diploma, OCR Cambridge Technical Extended Diploma, BTEC Subsidiary Diploma(s), Access to HE courses, Scottish Highers, and IB Diploma Programme. We also welcome applicants who are currently studying, or who've already gained a Foundation Diploma in Art and Design. Many EU and International qualifications are also accepted If you have any questions about our entry requirements, please contact our Admissions team at admissions@aub.ac.uk . English language requirements International students will need IELTS (academic or UKVI) of 6.0 overall, with a minimum of 5.5 in each component (reading, writing, speaking and listening). We accept a variety of national and international qualifications – for the full list, visit our English Language Requirements page . International Scholarships We aim to have a diverse student environment with the best creative talent in the UK. To support our goal of a multicultural campus, Arts University Bournemouth (AUB) is pleased to offer several awards which may come in the form of bursaries, fee waivers and scholarships. There will be a simple scholarship application form for you to complete. This form will be available to you after you receive an offer of admission from AUB. All AUB awards are offered on a first come, first served basis. If you do not qualify for a scholarship or bursary, you can take advantage of the Early Payment Fee Waiver, which is available to all who qualify. Each student will only qualify for one scholarship, bursary or fee waiver – they cannot be stacked. If a student is enrolled part-time, scholarships, bursaries, and fee waivers may be pro-rated to the yearly tuition fees. To help you plan and budget your finances during your time at AUB, as an international student, we've created a Cost of Living guide . If you'd like to discuss any of these financial awards or discuss any financial matters, get in touch with our International team who'll be able to help. Please note: all international scholarships are for on-campus courses only and do not apply to online courses. Arts University Bournemouth (AUB)  
Fees Payment Policy 2026/27 
Version: Final Institutional Draft 
Policy Owner: Finance Department 
Approval By: CFOO 
Approval Date: September 2026 
Review Cycle: Annual 
Next Review Date: February 2027 
 
Table of Contents 
 
1. Purpose ................................................................................................................................................................ ................. 2 
2. Scope ..................................................................................................................................................................................... 2 
3. Principles ............................................................................................................................................................................. 2 
4. Fee Liability ......................................................................................................................................................................... 2 
5. Fee Review and Variation .............................................................................................................................................. 2 
6.Tuition Fee Categories ..................................................................................................................................................... 3 
7.Student Loans Company (SLC) Funding .................................................................................................................. 3 
8. Payment Arrangements ................................................................................................................................................. 4 
9. Deposits ............................................................................................................................................................................... 4 
10.Payment Deadlines ........................................................................................................................................................ 5 
11. Refunds and Withdrawals .......................................................................................................................................... 5 
12. Escalation Process in Case of non-Payment ..................................................................................................... 6 
13. Governance and Monitoring ...................................................................................................................................... 8 
 
 
 
  
1. Purpose 
This policy sets out the framework governing tuition fee liability, payment expectations, 
refunds, and escalation procedures at Arts University Bournemouth (AUB). It ensures 
transparency for students and compliance with consumer protection legislation, 
Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) guidance, and regulatory expectations. 
It applies to all tuition, accommodation, library, and miscellaneous charges payable to 
AUB. The policy aims to ensure transparency, fairness, and responsible financial 
management while minimizing student debt. 
2. Scope 
This policy outlines the financial obligations of students at Arts University Bournemouth 
(AUB) and applies to all students enrolled on AUB provision including foundation, 
undergraduate, postgraduate, online, short course, and exchange programmes. 
3. Principles 
AUB administers fee collection according to the following principles: 
• Transparency of information prior to enrolment 
• Fair and consistent application of procedures 
• Compliance with consumer and contract law 
• Proportionate escalation of non-payment actions 
• Consideration of individual circumstances where engagement occurs 
4. Fee Liability 
Students become liable for tuition fees upon enrolment or acceptance of terms as defined 
within their student contract. Liability applies regardless of third- party sponsorship or 
funding delays. 
5. Fee Review and Variation 
AUB reviews its Fees Payment Policy annually and may amend it when necessary to reflect 
regulatory, financial, or operational changes. Tuition fees may also be adjusted in line with 
inflation and/or as permitted by the UK Government, including changes to t he maximum 
fee for Home Undergraduate degrees. If such changes take effect, the tuition fees you pay 
in future years of study may differ from those you paid in your current year. 
6.Tuition Fee Categories 
Tuition fee levels are determined by student residency status and course type. 
Student Status 
• Home Students : Tuition fees are set in accordance with UK Government 
regulations. AUB reserves the right to charge up to the maximum fee permitted 
under those regulations. 
• International Students : Tuition fees are determined by AUB and are reviewed 
annually. Fee levels may vary between academic years and will be confirmed in offer 
documentation. 
• Channel Islands and Isle of Man Students: Students from the Channel Islands and 
Isle of Man are charged tuition fees in line with Home fee structures. 
Foundation Courses 
• Home students who are under 19 years of age on 31 August in the year of course 
commencement are not required to pay tuition fees. 
• Students aged 19 or over, or those classified as International or Channel Islands and 
Isle of Man, are required to pay tuition fees. 
• Additional charges may apply for materials, resources, or registration, and these will 
be communicated in advance where relevant. 
Higher Education Courses (Full-time and Part-time) 
All students enrolled on Higher Education programmes are liable for tuition fees for each 
academic year of study, regardless of mode of attendance. 
Details of applicable fee levels are published on the AUB website and confirmed in 
individual offer documentation. For detailed tuition fee structures, visit:  
Foundation Fees 
Undergraduate Fees 
Postgraduate Fees 
Research Fees 
7.Student Loans Company (SLC) Funding 
• Undergraduate Tuition Fee Loans: Tuition fee loans provided by the Student Loans 
Company (SLC) for undergraduate study are paid directly to AUB on behalf of the 
student. 
• Maintenance Loans: Maintenance loans are paid directly to students by the SLC 
and are intended to support living costs. These funds are not applied toward tuition 
fees by AUB. 
• Postgraduate Loans : For Master’s and Postgraduate Research students, SLC 
funding is paid directly to the student. Students are responsible for ensuring that 
tuition fees are paid to AUB in accordance with the published payment schedule. 
• Students remain ultimately responsible for the payment of their tuition fees in full, 
regardless of the timing or status of SLC payments.  
For further information please visit: SLC Website 
8. Payment Arrangements 
AUB operates a cashless payment environment. Payments must be made via authorised 
online platforms. Instalment arrangements are communicated at enrolment and must be 
adhered to unless amended by agreement. Links to Payment portals are given as below: 
• Home & Online Students: Open Payment Pathway 
• International & Online Students: International Payment Portal 
• Short Courses: AUB Online Store 
Students from sanctioned countries must complete a Pre-Payment Advice form before 
transferring funds. 
9. Deposits 
Deposits listed as below will be required to secure a place or meet visa sponsorship 
requirements. Deposit conditions and refundability are communicated at offer stage. AUB 
reserves the right to change deposit requirements.  
• International Students (CAS Required): Deposit of one term’s tuition fees. 
• Nigeria & Pakistan Nationals: 50% of the full-year fee before CAS issuance. 
• International Masters students: £500 non-refundable acceptance deposit. 
• Online Masters students: £500 non-refundable acceptance fee. 
• US Federal Aid / Government Loan Recipients:  £500 non -refundable deposit (paid 
directly to AUB). 
• Students with Financial Guarantee Letters: No deposit required. 
 
10.Payment Deadlines 
Undergraduate & Postgraduate On-Campus Students 
• Termly instalments (3 equal payments): Due at the start of each term. 
Online Masters Students 
• Fees are payable in full at the start of the course. In exceptional circumstances, 
payment may be made in three equal instalments where this has been agreed in 
advance with AUB. 
• Students will not be able to enrol on the course until they have paid the £500 non-
refundable acceptance fee. Students have up to the end of the first taught week to 
pay the acceptance fee and enrol on the course. 
Short Courses / Summer Courses 
• Fees in full due at the time of booking. 
Study Abroad 
• Full payment upfront (or pre-arranged instalments in exceptional circumstances). 
 Accommodation Fees 
• Termly payments as per the tenancy agreement. 
11. Refunds and Withdrawals 
Refund eligibility is determined by withdrawal timing relative to teaching activity. 
Administrative deductions may apply. Refund rights are communicated clearly before 
enrolment. Accommodation refunds are governed separately by tenancy agreements. 
• On-campus provision  :Tuition fee liability is calculated based on the number of 
academic terms attended.  A student is deemed to have attended a term once the 
first taught week of that term has been completed. 
• Online MA (two -year provision) : Tuition fee liability is calculated based on the 
number of units commenced. A student is deemed to have commenced a unit once 
the first taught week of that unit has been completed. 
• International Administrative Fee : An administrative charge of £750 applies to 
international students who withdraw during Term 1. 
• Visa Refusal Refunds: Refunds following visa refusal are subject to a £100 
administrative fee . An additional charge of up to £1,500 may apply where the 
refusal results from incorrect or incomplete information provided by the student  or 
where the student declines their place at AUB. 
• Short Course Refunds: A full refund will be issued if withdrawal occurs within 14 
days of accepting the course offer (statutory cooling-off period). 
• A full refund will also be issued where withdrawal occurs 30 days or more prior to 
the course start date. 
Scholarships, Bursaries and Fee Waivers 
AUB offers a range of scholarships, bursaries, discounts, and fee incentives. Eligibility 
criteria, application processes, and full terms are published on the AUB website and may 
vary by academic year. 
• International Students: Eligible students may apply for AUB scholarships. An Early 
Payment Fee Waiver of £1,500 may be available where the full annual tuition fee is 
paid by 1 August. Further details are published under International Scholarships  – 
see link International Scholarships . There is no progression  discount for students 
repeating a year. 
• Post Graduate Students : Alumni and other eligible applicants may qualify for  
progression fee discounts. Full details are available within the published 
Postgraduate Fees information. Postgraduate Fees. 
• Short Course Discounts: Following discounts may apply, subject to availability and 
administered on a first-come basis: 
I. 20% discount for one student per course from Bournemouth University (BU), 
Bournemouth & Poole College (BPC), or residents of the Innovation Studio 
II. 20% discount for one AUB staff member per course 
III. 20% discount for one child of a current staff member for Saturday Art School 
All discounts are subject to eligibility verification and may not be combined unless explicitly 
stated. 
12. Escalation Process in Case of non-Payment 
On-Campus, BA Online, and Postgraduate Online (30 -week and 105 -week 
programmes) 
Where tuition or accommodation fees remain unpaid, AUB will follow a staged escalation 
process. Communications will normally be issued via multiple channels including email, 
text message, and student portal notifications. 
International students - If the fees detailed in the schedule below remain unpaid, your visa 
may be subject to curtailment. 
Step Tuition Fees Action Accommodation Fees Action

Reminder Notice 1 issued (Email and 
Text)

Where tuition fees remain unpaid, the following staged process applies: 
Step Action 
1 Day 8 — Reminder notice issued requesting immediate payment (Email and Text) 
2 Day 15 — Second reminder notice issued requesting immediate payment (Email 
and Text) 
3 Day 22 — Temporary block placed on the student account. Access will be 
restored once outstanding fees are settled 
4 Two weeks after Day 22 — Student withdrawn from the course if payment remains 
outstanding 
 
Students are strongly encouraged to contact the Finance Office at the earliest opportunity 
if they anticipate difficulty meeting payment obligations. Early engagement may allow 
alternative arrangements to be considered. 
Additional Consequences of Outstanding Fees 
• Students with unpaid fees will not normally be permitted to commence a 
subsequent term, re-enrol, graduate, or receive official academic documentation. 
• Students sponsored under the Student Route (formerly Tier 4)  visa may be 
withdrawn in line with UKVI compliance requirements, and changes to enrolment 
status may be reported to the Home Office where required. 
Students are encouraged to contact the Finance Office as early as possible if they 
experience difficulty meeting payment obligations. Engagement may enable supportive 
arrangements to be considered prior to escalation. 
Escalation actions are applied in accordance with institutional regulations and may affect 
progression, access to services, or contractual accommodation rights. 
AUB recognises individual financial circumstances and will handle each case sensitively. 
Students facing financial difficulties should contact the Finance Office immediately at 
income@aub.ac.uk. 
Exchange Programmes 
• AUB students on an Exchange Programme must pay full AUB tuition fees. 
• No additional tuition fees payable to the partner institution. 
• Exchange students may qualify for Maintenance & Travel Grants – contact 
international@aub.ac.uk. 
13. Governance and Monitoring 
The Finance D epartment monitors policy application and reports material risks or 
deviations through institutional governance channels.

MA Creative Teaching and Learning Design (Online) Mode of study: Part-time Study location: Online How to apply: Apply directly to us Overview Course details Studios and resources How to apply Overview The MA Creative Teaching and Learning Design course prepares you to be a learning professional with the knowledge and skills to design, deliver and lead transformative learning experiences. This comprehensive programme uniquely combines principles of creative education and research with advanced learning design, preparing you for leadership roles in learning and teaching. Register your interest Book a one-to-one How to apply Downloads Course specification Explore foundational concepts in learning and teaching. Master advanced application and research. Our approach recognises the complex interplay between creativity, pedagogy, and technology in modern learning environments. Our goal is to empower learning designers who can reimagine education for the 21st century. We believe great teaching and learning design can make a positive difference to people’s lives. Our MA is founded on our desire to empower our students to lead change through transformative learning experiences. And it’s built out of our extensive experience as professional educators and learning designers. MA Creative Writing offers a supportive, focused space in which to develop your professional writing practice, mentored by industry professionals. Take your writing to the next level while sharing the journey with fellow wordsmiths. This course may be studied full-time from September. *This course is subject to validation. Register your interest Book a one-to-one View our prospectus How to apply Downloads Course specification Develop your writing practice with an ethical, ecological mindset MA Creative Writing foregrounds ethics and ecology as intrinsic to the creative-critical practice of a situated, conscionable writer in the 21 st Century. This approach is articulated in the Future Ecologies framework, which underpins the course, and the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals, which are used to ensure relevance and engagement with the major challenges of the modern age. Learn in an area of natural beauty and rich literary heritage As a coastal university close to the UNESCO World Heritage Jurassic Coast, New Forest National Park, and Dorset National Landscape, AUB offers an inspiring, lively beach town location and base for writers seeking to connect with natural and cultural ecosystems in an area associated with many famous writers including Mary Shelley, John Le Carré, J.R.R. Tolkien, Sylvia Townsend Warner, and others. Chat to a student Our student ambassadors are here to answer any questions you might have on university life, our courses and all things AUB. The curriculum not only interrogates contemporary practices but also pioneers new ones, preparing graduates to lead in both existing and emerging fashion fields. At the forefront of growing digital demand Emerging technologies such as AR, artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning are seamlessly integrated into the curriculum, fostering an environment where digital artisanry meets design thinking and storytelling. Home Postgraduate Courses MA Film Practice (Online) MA Film Practice (Online) Mode of study: Part-time, online Study location: Online How to apply: Apply directly to us Overview Course details How to apply Showcase Course team Careers and industry Overview With our MA Film Practice (Online) course, you'll explore the possibilities of contemporary film and moving image practice. Register your interest Book a one-to-one How to apply Downloads Course specification Realise your creative ambitions in the context of an international learning community. You'll be supported in working across narrative fiction, documentary, experimental film, artist moving image, and hybrid projects. In addition to the online seminars and one-to-one tutorials, you also have access to live meeting with our Industry Patrons – one if whom Ania Trzebiatowska, a Los Angeles-based feature film programmer for the Sundance Film Festival – and bespoke recorded lectures by a range of extraordinary practitioners, including BAFTA-nominated film editor Nick Gibbon, BBC commissioned filmmaker Stella Scott, and international composer and sound designer Richy Carey. Question and debate established and mainstream modes of film practice. You'll be encouraged to think critically about your work and others', and to consider how film practice can engage with our contemporary world. In addition to guiding you in developing and realising your MA film or moving image work, you'll also be supported in presenting your work through film festivals, gallery exhibitions, and screening events. Current student work Want to get a sense of what you could achieve on MA Film Practice (Online)? Take a look at the work of current student Jonny White below. Jonny's film Still Moving (2025) is a four-minute, black-and-white poetic short exploring ageing and identity through contemporary dance. Home Postgraduate Courses MA Historical Costume MA Historical Costume Mode of study: Full-time Study location: AUB Campus How to apply: Apply directly to us Overview Course details Studios and resources How to apply Showcase Course team Careers and Industry Overview The MA Historical Costume course is designed to introduce students with a pre-existing interest in historical clothing to a range of historical costume practices and the fundamentals of research in the field of dress and costume history. It then encourages you to develop an individual specialism in the field that's aligned with your own artistic and professional aspirations, allowing you to demonstrate an advanced level of research and creative output within that specialism. This course can be studied full-time from September. Register your interest Book a one-to-one How to apply Downloads Course specification Develop a grounding in different approaches to historical costume. MA Historical Costume gives you the opportunity to explore archival research, historical making and costume design and styling. Sharpen practical, research and making skills. Student projects and interests fall into creative directions including costume for theatre and film, historical costume making, and curation and heritage. Course gallery Looking to be inspired? MA Innovation and Creative Entrepreneurship is for people who want to make a change. This course will enable you to identify open problems and the appropriate frameworks to develop evidence-based responses, and work on live projects with external partners. This course can be studied full-time from September. Register your interest Book a one-to-one How to apply Downloads Course specification Gain the skills and confidence to launch your own innovative project. You'll work with external partners on live projects, applying your ongoing learning as you develop your innovative and entrepreneurial mindset. Home Postgraduate Courses MA Photography (Online) MA Photography (Online) Mode of study: Part-time Study location: Online How to apply: Apply directly to us Overview Course details How to apply Showcase Course team Careers and industry Overview The MA Photography (Online) course at Arts University Bournemouth is a part-time flexible course that integrates practice and theory through intensive online study. The course will offer you an opportunity to develop and realise your creative ambitions while exploring new approaches to your photographic practice. You'll work in the context of an international learning community that foregrounds peer feedback and research driven experimentation. Throughout, you'll be encouraged to apply thinking through practice in ways that respond to the contemporary world and question established mainstream modes of photographic practice. The experiences and knowledge that each of you bring are central to the course as you dynamically expand your body of work during a series of structured creative projects. You'll be encouraged to critically interrogate your practice through bespoke mentorship ultimately leading to the conceptualisation and manifestation of your final thesis project. Image: Anthony Chris Schmidt Register your interest Book a one-to-one How to apply Downloads Course specification What is Photography now? The course recognises and celebrates an expansive and progressive understanding and definition of photography, its audiences and the sites and contexts in which it can be presented. During the course you may choose to experiment with different photographic modes (including but not exclusively) documentary, fashion, street, still life, landscape, fine art or other works that emphasise innovation and a commitment to examining form and content. Online and flexible The course is designed to be highly flexible, utilising an online delivery mode that brings practitioners together with distinct interests and cultural perspectives. It's designed for students that want to maintain continuity in their professional and personal lives while refining a creative methodology and enhancing career prospects in their chosen specialism over the two-year period of study. At the beginning of the course, you'll explore and develop your creative point of view by reviewing earlier practice, positioning your work by understanding relevant fields or references, and establishing a reflective journal. You'll then join a carousel of seven individual 15-credit units, each fostering distinct processes of making, thinking, and reflecting through short practice based, research led projects. In the second year of the course, you'll begin to work towards your final thesis project. You'll be supported in conceptualising and communicating your intentions in a detailed proposal in preparation for the resolution phase in which you will receive more individual supervision and support. Home Postgraduate Courses MA Transformative Learning MA Transformative Learning Currently viewing: Show contents Path 3 Created with Sketch. Overview MA Transformative Learning offers a distinctive approach to postgraduate study, drawing on the tradition of holistic science to reimagine ways of knowing and being through an integration of artistic practice, scientific observation and philosophical inquiry. This course is delivered by Ruskin Mill Centre for Practice (RMCP) from Emerson College and the George Adams Centre , and validated by Arts University Bournemouth (AUB). Visit Ruskin Mill Centre for Practice's website Downloads Course specification MA Transformative Learning course information On the MA Transformative Learning course, you’ll experience transformation firsthand through an immersive exploration of diverse subjects, developing a deep understanding of how learning itself can become transformative. In a rich curriculum that includes hands-on investigations of light, colour, projective geometry, plant morphology, animal ecology, poetic language and musical traditions, the course provides you with an opportunity to: Develop multiple ways of seeing – learning to observe and understand the world from multiple perspectives. Integrate artistic, scientific and philosophical approaches into a holistic understanding. Nurture an ecological awareness – developing deeper connections with the natural world. Explore the evolution of consciousness – how human experience has changed throughout history. Apply transformative approaches in diverse contexts – from educational settings to environmental organisations, healthcare, social enterprises, cultural institutions, and organisational change. Develop research skills that advance transformative practice – creating new knowledge through your own investigations. The immersive dialogue between diverse ways of knowing will equip you with skills to challenge dominant narratives, prevailing worldviews and established frameworks of understanding, providing a basis to develop innovative approaches that respond to our changing world. Course philosophy Course outline Course philosophy RMCP recognises students as individuals with distinct personal and career aspirations. We provide challenging opportunities for deep engagement with their chosen fields, encouraging critical assessment of practice within creative, economic, and cultural contexts. We foster interdisciplinary collaboration, blending theory and practice and our ethos equips students with skills to navigate significant social, political, economic and ecological changes. We aim to produce graduates who not only pursue careers but help redefine employment in these transformative times. Course outline The course moves through five integrated units over three years: Holistic Ways of Seeing establishes foundational approaches through direct engagement with natural phenomena. The Living World develops understanding through engagement with practice of making and careful observation of plant form. Organism and Environment explores co-evolutionary relationships between living organisms and their ecological contexts. Evolution of Consciousness examines the interplay between human consciousness and cultural development, providing a foundation for understanding learning’s transformative potential. Researching Transformative Learning supports the development and application of original contributions to the field of transformative learning. As students, you'll learn through: Field-based investigation in natural settings Studio practice developing observational skills Research seminars exploring critical and philosophical thinking Craft workshops for developing interdisciplinary understanding and professional capabilities Individual projects applying learning to practice i i i i How to apply When you're ready to apply, you'll need to head to our online application form to apply directly to us. We encourage you to apply early to secure your place. We encourage applications from students with a broad range of qualifications and experiences. We'll take into consideration the knowledge and skills that have been developed inside and outside the classroom, as well as your previous qualifications. No portfolio is required for this course. Please note: once you've applied to AUB, your application will be shared with RMCP, who'll continue the admissions process, including arranging interviews. Register your interest Book an Open day Order our prospectus How to apply Downloads Course Specification Challenge perceptions and expectations. Register your interest Open Days Order our prospectus How to apply Downloads Course Specification Explore key facets of impactful communication design. BA (Hons) Content Creation with Marketing Duration: 3–5 years full-time Placement year: Optional 1 year Course code: W225 (UCAS) Institution code: A66 (UCAS) Overview Course details Studios and resources How to apply Course team Careers and industry Overview BA (Hons) Content Creation with Marketing offers a practical degree that takes an authentic approach to your learning enabling you to develop and hone your skills in developing compelling digital content for a range of online platforms. In tandem with content creation, you'll learn about the business and strategy of digital production, including how to work with data sets, manage finance and develop short-, medium- and long-term strategies to enable businesses to use content creation to drive engagement, sales and consumer loyalty. Register your interest Open Days Order our prospectus How to apply Downloads Course Specification Analyse audiences. Plan, produce and evaluate content. Learn how to strategise for short-, medium- and longer-term business planning for digital content to enable brands to meet their goals and work across platforms. We're professionally accredited. This course is accredited by the Chartered Management Institute (CMI). In addition to your BA (Hons) degree, you'll also graduate with a CMI Level 5 qualification and Foundation Chartered Manager (fCMgr) status. Register your interest Book an Open Day Order our prospectus How to apply Downloads Course Specification Our approach encourages students to break boundaries and tell stories that truly resonate. You'll develop the skills, knowledge, and professional mindset to thrive in the competitive and evolving costume industry. Join the UK's largest film school outside London Our unique teaching and learning model places you in real-world production settings, allowing you, as costume makers and designers to work closely with aspiring directors, producers, writers, actors and make-up artists. Watch our videos Final-year student Daisy talks about going from self-taught sewing to discovering the art of millinery on BA (Hons) Costume. You can also hear from award-winning alumni Sophie Canale ( Saltburn, Bridgerton ) and Eleanor Bull ( Poor Things ) about their respective experiences on the course and working in industry. In addition, you can hear several students sharing their experiences working and collaborating in different costume roles on AUB Theatre Productions shows. Home Undergraduate Courses BA (Hons) Fashion BA (Hons) Fashion Duration: 3–5 years full-time Placement year: Optional 1 year Course code: W230 (UCAS) Institution code: A66 (UCAS) Overview Course details Studios and resources How to apply Showcase Course team Careers and industry Overview BA (Hons) Fashion merges traditional skills and craftsmanship with contemporary, cutting-edge technology and ethical practice. You'll interrogate the current industry while creating innovative, sustainable and bold garments of your own. Register Your Interest Book an Open Day Order our prospectus How to apply Downloads Course Specification Join an award-winning fashion course. BA (Hons) Fashion are award-winners in fashion innovation. The AUB Fashion community supports experimentation, exploration and the application of traditional and contemporary techniques and methods, to inform creative solutions for a more considered fashion future. Explore and experiment towards a more considered fashion future. From concept to realisation, you'll experiment, interrogate, and develop design practices appropriate to their individual design philosophy. You'll creatively discover design practice, cutting-edge digital fashion technology, craftsmanship, product development and presentation. You'll also explore connections between concepts of dress, fashion, and the body as a site for artistic expression. Watch our course videos Find out from current student Maeve and recent graduate Jason about what it’s like to study BA (Hons) Fashion at AUB. Also, catch a snippet of some of our 2025 graduating students' work on the runway at Graduate Fashion Week. Home Undergraduate Courses BA (Hons) Fine Art BA (Hons) Fine Art Duration: 3–5 years full-time Placement year: Optional 1 year Course code: W100 (UCAS) Institution code: A66 (UCAS) Overview Course details Studios and resources How to apply Showcase Course team Careers and industry Overview Be part of an exciting, multi-discipline BA (Hons) Fine Art course, set within our dynamic culture of making in our purpose-built studios. We take great pride in our course to create a thriving fine art community. Explore current student artwork on our course Instagram: @aubfineart Register your interest Book an Open Day Order our prospectus How to apply Downloads Course Specification Consider fine art in its widest sense. On BA (Hons) Fine Art at AUB, you'll have the freedom to test out many different approaches to your artistic practice and to refine your way of working. The course team have learnt that fine art making and problem-solving skills are transferable to wide-ranging career pathways – these range from being an artist, an educator or creative entrepreneurial business opportunities. The course aims to nurture well-rounded, creatively confident individuals who are flexible in their outlook to employment opportunities. Experiment to find your medium. Experimental workshops in painting, drawing, printmaking and sculpture provide you with a solid foundation in testing the physical and conceptual potential of materials that you can then develop further. Watch our course videos Discover from students Gio, Madeleine and Ella about what it's like to study BA (Hons) Fine Art at AUB. In addition, Jennifer Anyan (Director of School of Arts, Media and Creative Industries Management) sits down with Professor Elizabeth Price and discusses the trajectory of her wide and varied artistic career. Price is a major figure in contemporary art in Britain, having won the Turner Prize in 2012. She has exhibited internationally at major galleries and museums, and has worked as a professor and lecturer at a number of arts universities in the UK. Home Undergraduate Courses BA (Hons) Graphic Design BA (Hons) Graphic Design Duration: 3–5 years full-time Placement year: Optional 1 year Course code: W210 (UCAS) Institution code: A66 (UCAS) Overview Course details Studios and resources How to apply Showcase Course team Careers and industry Overview Thinking through making is core to the BA (Hons) Graphic Design course. "Bringing ideas to life" involves taking a concept or thought and turning it into a tangible reality or action that's expressed through creativity, innovation, and craft. This approach promotes design practice as a conversation, not a monologue, where you're encouraged to work with one another collaboratively on set and industry-led projects. Register your interest Book an Open Day Order our prospectus How to apply Downloads Course Specification Benefit from deep professional and practical knowledge. BA (Hons) Graphic Design at AUB is driven by passion for conceptually led projects and collaboration with industry partners. Embrace innovative technologies and address design challenges. You'll learn to respond ethically, with curiosity, and strategically to new challenges such as climate emergency, social injustice, economic inequality, and cultural development. Watch our course videos Find out from students Gabby, Paul and Nayanika about what it’s like to study BA (Hons) Graphic Design at AUB. Home Undergraduate Courses BA (Hons) Makeup, Hair and Prosthetics BA (Hons) Makeup, Hair and Prosthetics Duration: 3–5 years full-time Placement year: Optional 1 year Course code: W45G (UCAS) Institution code: A66 (UCAS) Overview Course details Studios and resources How to apply Showcase Course team Careers and industry Overview BA (Hons) Makeup, Hair and Prosthetics equips you with the creative, technical, and professional skills required to work as a makeup artist across a range of creative industries. From the outset, you’ll build strong foundations in makeup, hair, prosthetics, wigs, and postiche, while developing analytical, research, and communication skills essential for professional practice. In your final year, you’ll define and develop your individual specialisms through independent projects, research, and professional collaborations. You’ll be encouraged to take creative risks, demonstrate intellectual and artistic integrity, and build a distinctive portfolio that reflects your ambitions. Seize the opportunity to study at a place where creativity, collaboration, and innovation come together. Register your interest Book an Open Day Order our prospectus How to apply Downloads Course Specification Refine your technical abilities and explore makeup within industry-focused environments. Live projects in film, performance, photography, and events will enhance your employability, while digital technologies and contextual studies support your ability to develop character transformation through creative design and application. Join the UK's largest film school outside London. The makeup artist is an important member of any production team. You’ll work with your peers studying acting, film production, and costume to create ‘live’ collaborative projects within Bournemouth Film School. Home Undergraduate Courses BA (Hons) Textiles Design BA (Hons) Textiles Design Duration: 3–5 years full-time Placement year: Optional 1 year Course code: W236 (UCAS) Institution code: A66 (UCAS) Overview Course details Studios and resources How to apply Showcase Course team Careers and industry Overview BA (Hons) Textiles Design will encourage you to fully embrace colour, pattern and texture in the production of both hard and soft surfaces; for both fashion and interiors. Core to course delivery are experimentation with drawing, dye techniques, print, stitch, constructed textiles and knit. Textiles surround us – it’s one of the largest design skill sets used globally. Register your interest Book an Open Day Order our prospectus How to apply Downloads Course Specification Explore the parameters of textiles design for both interiors and fashion. You'll interrogate long-standing textiles design traditions, question existing processes and create new ways of working, setting you up to confidently become part of the next generation of distinctive, skilled and inventive designers and makers. Examine textiles in their widest sense. The course emphasises individual exploration of both visual and theoretical principles in the investigation of colour, texture and pattern. You'll experiment with drawing, dye, print, stitch, CAD, fabric construction and manipulation, towards the development of tactile materials found within the discipline of textiles. Watch our videos Find out from student Catherine about what it’s like to study BA (Hons) Textiles Design at AUB. BA/BSc (Hons) Arts, Media and Creative Industries Management* Duration: 3 or 4 years full-time Placement year: Optional 1 year Course code: To be confirmed (UCAS) Institution code: A66 (UCAS) Overview Course details Studios and resources How to apply Course team Careers and industry Overview This course will run from September 2027. BA/BSc (Hons) Arts, Media and Creative Industries Management responds to the growing global demand for agile, business-savvy professionals in the creative industries. With a strong focus on leadership, innovation, and international collaboration, it equips students to shape impactful careers in a rapidly evolving cultural and media landscape. * This course is subject to validation. Register your interest Book an Open Day Order our prospectus How to apply Downloads Course Specification Find your place in strategic roles. Whether your background is in performance, visual arts, or media, BA/BSc (Hons) Arts, Media and Creative Industries Management supports your transition into strategic roles where creativity meets commerce. Learn to lead, launch and respond. Through a blend of practical and theoretical study, you’ll gain the tools to become a confident, values-led manager – ready to lead teams, launch ventures, and respond to the challenges facing creative organisations today. BSc (Hons) Fashion Management and Strategy Duration: 3–5 years full-time Placement year: Optional 1 year Course code: W112 (UCAS) Institution code: A66 (UCAS) Overview Course details Studios and resources How to apply Course team Careers and industry Overview This course will run from September 2027. BSc (Hons) Fashion Management and Strategy offers a rigorous values-based business management degree with a focused application for the fashion and lifestyle industries, giving you the skills you need to become a considered and ethical future leader in these exciting global industries. Register your interest Book an Open Day Order our prospectus How to apply Downloads Course Specification Develop strategy. Manage business. Consider impact. Develop your knowledge and skills in developing strategy for and managing business with a values-based approach, considering the impact on people, animals and the environment alongside understanding what it takes for a business to be creatively and financially successful. We're professionally accredited. This course is accredited by the Chartered Management Institute (CMI). In addition to your BA (Hons) degree, you'll also graduate with a CMI Level 5 qualification and Foundation Chartered Manager (fCMgr) status.
